sections.h2: What is Sumter County, South Carolina, and how did it start?
sections.html:
Sumter County is a central South Carolina county of about 682 square miles, with the city of Sumter as its seat and largest community. The Black River and its tributaries drain it, the Wateree River forms its western border, and it is one of five counties on Lake Marion (Wikipedia).

Sumter District was formed in 1798 from parts of Clarendon, Claremont and Salem counties and named for General Thomas Sumter. It became Sumter County under the 1868 Constitution. A fire in 1801 destroyed the early county records, and boundaries shifted again in 1902, when part went to form Lee County, and in 1921, when a section came from Clarendon County.

Those boundary changes matter to old deeds. If you are selling inherited land with a legal description from the early or mid 1900s, a title company may need to trace which county recorded it.

sections.h2: Which neighboring counties and natural areas surround it?
sections.html:
Lee lies to the north, Florence to the northeast, Clarendon to the south, Calhoun to the southwest, Richland to the west and Kershaw to the northwest. The county holds Poinsett State Park, part of Woods Bay State Park and part of Manchester State Forest, and the High Hills of Santee rise in the west.

Land near the Wateree, the Black River swamps and Lake Marion can carry flood and moisture risk, so ask the county or the seller's insurer about flood zones before you rely on a house being easy to insure.

sections.h2: What do Shaw Air Force Base and other employers mean for homeowners?
sections.html:
Shaw Air Force Base is the county's best-known installation and opened in 1941. According to Wikipedia it hosts the headquarters of the 9th Air Force, AFCENT and U.S. Army Central, among other units, and the city's page notes that the base is home to the 20th Fighter Wing.

Manufacturing is the largest employment sector at about 18%, ahead of health care and retail. Named employers include Becton Dickinson, Central Carolina Technical College, the City of Sumter, Continental AG, the Department of Defense, Eaton, SKF, Pilgrim's Pride, Prisma Health, Speedway and Walmart. County gross domestic product for 2022 was about $5 billion.

Military families move on assignment, and a household that receives orders may have little time to sell. In September 2024 the National Park Service named Sumter and Sumter County jointly a World War II Heritage City.

sections.h2: What is the city of Sumter like, in numbers?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 43,463 people in the city and 105,556 in the county. The city's page lists a median age of 35.3 years.

Public high schools are Crestwood, Lakewood and Sumter. Higher education includes Morris College, Central Carolina Technical College and the University of South Carolina Sumter. Columbia is about 45 miles to the west.

sections.h2: What does the weather mean for a Sumter house?
sections.html:
Sumter has a humid subtropical climate with long, hot summers. The mean daily high is about 55 degrees in January and about 90 in July, the record high is 105 and the record low is 2.

July is the wettest month, with about 5.75 inches. Heat and humidity put steady load on air conditioners, roofs and wood framing. If a house has an older HVAC system, mention its age to the buyer instead of leaving them to find out at inspection.

sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Sumter County?
sections.html:
The Assessor and the Treasurer share an address at 13 East Canal Street, Sumter, SC 29150, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. The county main line is 803-436-2102, and the Treasurer's delinquent tax page lists 803-436-2213.

The county's assessor FAQ shows a Treasurer number of 803-436-2216, so the county pages list more than one number. If one rings through, ask for the Treasurer and note the number that works.

sections.h2: When is Sumter County property tax due?
sections.html:
Notices go out each October and are due January 15 without penalty. The county's payment page gives the penalty steps.

Payment dateAdded to base tax
After January 153%
After February 110%
After March 1615%

Online payments run through the county's qpaybill system. The county warns that its online services pages may not include added penalties and fees, so confirm the payoff with the Treasurer.

State law lets a county council allow installment payments by ordinance (S.C. Code 12-45-75). We found nothing confirming that Sumter County does, so ask the Treasurer.

sections.h2: What assessment rules and exemptions apply?
sections.html:
An owner-occupied home that is the owner's legal residence is assessed at 4%, and other residential property at 6%. Apply with the Assessor as soon as you move in, and tell the Assessor within 30 days if the home stops being your domicile.

  • Reassessment increases are capped at 15% for tax purposes.
  • The Assessor mails a notice when fair market value rises by $1,000 or more.
  • Homestead exemption: residents who are 65 or older, totally disabled or legally blind, with one year of South Carolina residency, exclude the first $50,000 of the legal residence's value. Apply at the County Auditor's Office.
  • Some disabled veterans and surviving spouses of service members killed in the line of duty may be exempt on the home and up to five acres, through the SC Department of Revenue.

The county's FAQ page still lists 2016 as the next reassessment, which is out of date, so ask the Assessor for the current cycle.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Sumter County assessment?
sections.html:
File a written appeal with the County Assessor within 90 days of the assessment notice date, without waiting for the tax bill.

  1. If the appeal is unresolved by December 31, you are billed at least 80% of the current assessed value.
  2. You may ask in writing to be billed more than 80% to avoid interest if you lose.
  3. Taxes are due January 15 regardless.
  4. After resolution you receive a refund or owe the difference plus interest.

Appeals of Department of Revenue assessments follow their own 90-day protest rule and are a separate track.

sections.h2: When is the Sumter County tax sale?
sections.html:
The county's Treasurer page says the delinquent tax sale is on December 8, 2026. Real estate and mobile home taxes must be paid by 5 p.m. on December 7, 2026 to avoid sale, and bidder registration closes November 20, 2026.

The county's payment page describes the annual sale as held the first Monday of November, which does not match, so confirm the date with the Treasurer.

State law gives a 12-month redemption window with interest of 3%, 6%, 9% or 12% depending on the quarter (S.C. Code 12-51-90), and requires a certified mail notice 45 to 20 days before the period ends.

sections.h2: What should you do before selling a Sumter County house with tax due?
sections.html:
• Get a written payoff from the Treasurer, including penalties.
  • Check whether the sale date has passed or is close.
  • Ask whether the home is classed as your legal residence at 4%, and fix that if it is wrong.
  • Compare the sale price to the assessment if a reappraisal notice arrived.

faqs.q: When are Sumter County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due by January 15 without penalty. The county adds 3% after January 15, 10% after February 1 and 15% after March 16.

faqs.q: When is the Sumter County tax sale?
faqs.a: The county's Treasurer page lists December 8, 2026, with payment due by 5 p.m. on December 7 and bidder registration closing November 20. Another county page mentions the first Monday of November, so confirm with the Treasurer at 803-436-2213.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Sumter County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 90 days from the date on the assessment notice. File in writing with the Assessor, and pay on time because an appeal does not delay the due date.

faqs.q: What is the legal residence rate in Sumter County?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied homes that are the owner's legal residence are assessed at 4%, and other residential property at 6%. You apply through the Assessor.
